questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I am originally from Norway and wanted to experience how it was to work in the Norwegian healthcare system compared to the Danish one.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I thought it was rather difficult in the beginning, when filling out the application both in mobility and on the host university site, to understand what I needed to fill out, and when I would get answers and confirmations. It took a long time before I felt that everything was in place, and I did not receive information about which the departments I would attend, until about a week before arriving. But in the end, everything worked out, and I had contact with my Erasmus coordinator at the host university all through.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I met with my coordinator the week before I started, to welcome me and discuss any concerns I had. And every time I started a new rotation, I was met by someone who showed me how to get to the department and where the morning meetings were held.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I stayed with one of my childhood friends who already had an apartment in Oslo.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There is not really any campus housing associated with the hospitals, but there are other student housing you can apply for through SiO.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not make use of any student housing.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I do not remember the details of the process, but I do remember that my friends and I all had troubles and frustrations about the registration.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Sending emails to various exchange coordinators.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: There was only one option, clinical rotations.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It all works out in the end.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Clinical rotation, no other courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There were no classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Clinical rotations. 
(Thoraxkirurgisk, børnekirurgisk, radiologisk, ortopædisk, anæstesi)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Clinical rotations. 
I recommend Børnekirurgisk at Rikshospitalet and ortopædisk and anæstesi at Ullevål sykehus. They were all very inclusive, and great places to get to assist during surgeries and manage airways, as well as observe the trauma team at Ullevåls traumecenter.

questions.answer: Nothing unexpected

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food in general and alcohol is more expensive in Norway, but a pass for public transport for a month is cheaper (about 300 dkk).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Did not try any.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do not know.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Hiking, and skiing if the conditions allow it, in the nature surrounding Oslo. There are many small cabins/cafes in the forrest you can hike to, and enjoy a cinnamon bun and a coffee.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: See above.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy as I grew up in Norway.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: There were no other students at any of the departments I attended, I mostly socialized with friends I already knew in Oslo.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Hiking, nature.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: There were no other students at any of the departments I attended, so it can be difficult to meet other people your age at the hospital, especially if you change departments several times a month as I did. I already knew a lot of people in the city, but if you dont, then it would probably be smart to join some sort of student organization or group to meet others.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Contact your erasmus coordinator if you have any troubles with the application process.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to experience how life is at Norwegian hospitals, and getting to see my family and friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having to go all summer without knowing which hospitals and departments I would be attending, and only receiving information about where I would start a week before the exchange began.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I got to go to 5-6 different departments over the 12 week period, which was great because I got to see many different specialties. However, it is a more straining to be new to a hospital and ward so often, and I think you will be given even more responsibility if you stay in one place longer, and get to know both the doctors and the nurses better.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
